subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the values of t for which the points (t,2t), (2t,6t) and (3,8) are collinear.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Very Short Answer question 25, book p.143. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. NOTE ON THE ANSWER SET: t = 0 makes the first two points coincide at the origin, so the three points are collinear in the degenerate sense; it is a genuine root of the printed condition and is reported, with the coincidence stated on the page rather than quietly dropped. recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say which condition you write down for three collinear points, and how many values of t you expect.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the collinearity condition
steps.margin_note: First mark. Three points are collinear exactly when the triangle they form has zero area, so the area determinant is set to 0 before any algebra starts.
steps.memory_tip: Collinear means the triangle has zero area. Write the area expression and set it to 0.
lines: ⇒ x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂) = 0

recall.must_convey: That collinearity is written as the area of the triangle being zero.
accept: three collinear points make a triangle of zero area
set the area expression equal to zero
use x one into y two minus y three and so on
area zero ante collinear ani artham
heard_as: x one y two minus y three

steps.why: Any test for collinearity works, but the area form takes all three points at once and never divides by a difference, so it cannot break when two x-coordinates are equal.
common_mistakes: Equating only two slopes and dividing by (2t − t), which is zero when t = 0.
Writing the area as one half of the expression and then forgetting it is set to zero.

steps.label: Solve for t
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The expression factorises as 2t(t − 2), so there are two roots. Cancelling the t instead of factorising is what loses the mark.
steps.memory_tip: 2t(t − 2) = 0 has TWO roots. Never cancel the t — that throws away t = 0.
lines: At t = 0 both A and B become (0, 0), so the
three points still lie on one line.

recall.must_convey: That the condition reduces to 2t(t − 2) = 0, giving t = 0 and t = 2.
accept: two t into t minus two equals zero
t is zero or t is two
rendu values vastayi zero and two
heard_as: two t into t minus two

steps.why: At t = 2 the three points are genuinely different and lie on a line of slope 4. At t = 0 the first two points are the same point, and any three points of which two coincide lie on a line, so t = 0 also satisfies the condition as printed.
common_mistakes: Cancelling t and reporting only t = 2.
Making a sign slip in 3(2t − 6t) and getting a wrong quadratic.
